answer: Asynchronous Burst Jitter Sequencing forces every communicating node to execute pseudo-random micro-pauses before transmitting packets. Like an unpredictable ocean tide, these variable delays break synchronization across automated botnets. An attacker spinning up clones must forge timing signatures independently for each thread, leaking CPU cycles and memory. If a cluster attempts parallel flood attacks, the mandatory idle windows cause packets to wander outside valid delivery windows, instantly dropping fraudulent identities without consuming global stakes.
